# Repo registry and client-site naming

A new agent has access to **all** of these through the **GitHub connector** (the `gh` CLI and/or the GitHub MCP) — Adam authorizes that access, so you can read any repo here for prior patterns, conventions, or his workflow without him pasting code. Run `gh repo list AdamMirmina` to confirm the live list, and pull files with the connector. When you're looking for "how does Adam usually do X," these are the reference.

### Client-site repo naming: `<businessnamesquashed>-<realtld>`

Decided 2026-07-03. Every Ramsgate client-site repo (the ones living under `dev/clients/`) is named by squashing the business name to one word — no internal hyphens or spaces — then appending the client's **actual registered domain TLD**, not a hardcoded `-com`: `triciaelliott-com`, `planetarysolutions-net`, `camillegardella-com`. This replaces the older, inconsistent pattern (`triciaelliott-site`, `planetary-solutions-site`, bare `camille-gardella`). **Executed 2026-07-03**: all three existing client repos renamed on GitHub (`gh repo rename`) and local `origin` remotes repointed to match. Cloudflare Pages (planetary-solutions-site project) and the Vercel git integration (triciaelliott-site project) both track a repo by ID, not name, so both stayed connected through the rename with no redeploy needed. Deliberately left deploy-side identifiers alone (the Cloudflare Pages project name, the Vercel project name, and the `camille-gardella-site` Cloudflare Worker script name in `camillegardella-com`'s `wrangler.jsonc`) — the naming convention governs GitHub repo names, not live infra identifiers, and renaming a Worker script risks detaching its custom-domain route on a live client site for zero functional benefit. Revisit only as a deliberate, separately-verified task if full consistency is wanted.

**Corrected 2026-07-18:** the original 2026-07-03 execution defaulted every client repo to `-com` without checking each client's actual registered domain — Planetary Solutions' real domain is `planetarysolutions.net` (a `.net`, not `.com`), so `planetarysolutions-com` was simply wrong from day one. Adam caught it and had it renamed to `planetarysolutions-net` (GitHub rename + local clone repointed; the old local folder couldn't be removed in the same session because the harness pins that path as the session's working directory for its lifetime — it was left for a follow-up cleanup once freed). **The rule going forward: always verify the client's real domain TLD before naming or renaming a client-site repo — never assume `-com`.**

**Corrected 2026-08-11, a different edge case than the TLD one above:** "squash the business name to one word — no internal hyphens" is the right default when the client's real domain ALSO has no internal hyphen (`triciaelliott.com`, `camillegardella.com` — squashing loses nothing, since there was nothing to preserve). It's the wrong call when the client's actual registered domain keeps a hyphen as part of its own identity — `pioneering-space.com` for the Pioneering Space repo was first named `pioneeringspace-com` (squashed per the letter of the rule) and Adam caught it immediately: "shouldn't it be pioneering-space-com." Renamed. **The real rule underneath both corrections: the repo name should let you reconstruct the actual domain by eye — verify the domain's real hyphenation the same way you verify its real TLD, don't assume either.**
